attributes.law_screen: claim.law.PC_a-named-pointer-local-selects-the-displacement-load-and-its-declaration-site-decides-the-hoist.20260902.v1 SCREENED and found OUT OF SCOPE BY ITS OWN SCOPE CLAUSE, read literally. Its scope reads 'a memory reference whose address is a base register plus a SCALED INDEX plus a compile-time constant ... Says nothing about references with no scaled index.' Both sites the law was proven at (probes D and E of the superseded record) carry a genuine scaled index -- `i * PREC_STRIDE` and `k * PREC_STRIDE`. A `p = PT(0)` LOOP HEAD has index literal 0, i.e. NO scaled index at all, so the mandated hypothesis extrapolated the law past a boundary the law itself draws. This is a ZERO-BUILD refutation available before the first probe, and probe H then confirmed it empirically (NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL). claim.law.constant-copy-vs-rematerialize-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v1 SCREENED and read LITERALLY as the brief required, and CONFIRMED OUT OF SCOPE, agreeing with the superseded record: its scope demands 'two locals take the same small integer CONSTANT' with 'target-only +1 mr or +1 addi against ours-only -1 li'. Here the value is a relocated ADDRESS base, no `li` appears in the delta at all, and the direction is inverted (target has the addi, ours the mr). Treating it as a veto would have closed this run's only accepted axis, exactly the run-37 failure mode the brief warned of. claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1 SCREENED and OUT OF SCOPE for the same literal reason: it is scoped to a ZERO-VALUED register, not an address base. Its diagnosis nevertheless transfers as a prior and is cited in the new law. claim.law.cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base.20260831.v1 SCREENED, scope clause OUT (it governs 'a single element's field cluster' and names the LOOP-pointer laws as the companion cases), but its CRITICAL PROCEDURE clause -- that the conversion is all-or-nothing and partial conversions no-op or regress -- was taken as transferable diagnosis and is what motivated probe I over another single-site probe. That was the right call: the all-or-nothing form did move the stream where two single-site probes could not. claim.law.PL_permutation-pin-freezes-every-function-preceding-it-in-source-order.20260901.v1 APPLIED and HELD on both count-changing probes (I and J); each aborted the WEBFRANK stage on do_exit and each was cleared with wf_rederive_pin --transient returning ALL FOUR body hashes unchanged, which is the audit. claim.law.PC_real-and-multiset-agreement-does-not-license-a-keep-without-fresh-fuzzy.20260902.v1 and claim.law.IH_multiset-gain-does-not-imply-fuzzy-gain-arbitrate-with-count-distance.20260901.v1 SCREENED and both decisive: probes I and J each reached an EXACT instruction count with a 14t -> 12t multiset gain and fresh fuzzy rejected both. claim.law.real-can-underweight-a-large-alignment-gain SCREENED via probe.py's slot map, which is what re-surfaced the save-set delta.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Re-apply probe L (external linkage + the 0x14 pad) and dump the relocation SYMBOLS of the six demoted functions (DoPlayerTexMods, GetMaxPlayerModelSize, SetPlayerWindows, SetupPlayerTexMods, ShowRuneStones, del_player_blits) against the retail object's own relocation entries -- NOT against fnasm's target column, which is symbolized from config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt and cannot answer this. If the retail relocations name the SECTION symbol for those six, the external form is wrong for this TU and the whole axis is closed as a trade that can never net positive; if they name the object, the six are reconstruction debt and the axis is a live project win.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no - and this is the load-bearing caveat. The premise that first motivated probe K ('the target relocation names potionicon_tab while ours names the section symbol') was WRONG: fnasm's target column annotates retail addresses from symbols.txt and shows no real relocations, because the retail DOL has none. The codegen effect measured is real and reproducible (+0.2998 fuzzy, twin pair closed, 13 and then 7 sibling deltas), but it was found for a false reason and has NOT been screened against any real retail relocation evidence. Screen it before spending a probe.
hypothesis.statement: The linkage of the base object is a live codegen lever for this residual and it is the only axis measured this run that fuzzy ACCEPTED. Giving `potionicon_tab` external linkage (probe K, a one-word edit touching no function body) moved do_players from fuzzy 97.2692 to 97.5690 and CLOSED the twin j-loop `lwz`/`lwzx` pair at +0xef8/+0xfd4 outright -- the exact residual the superseded record declared CLOSED and source-exhausted after three declaration forms. It was reverted only because the full build gate showed the TU paying for it elsewhere: matched 66.43 -> 66.15, STRICT 2575 -> 2566 fns. The untried work is to SEPARATE the two effects. Probe L already proved they ARE separable in part: a 0x14 static pad restoring the sibling .bss run cut the damage from 13 regressions to 7 and turned abort_player 102 -> 96, inactivate_player 30 -> 24 and kill_player 32 -> 26 into IMPROVEMENTS. The 6 that remain are all `EXACT -> OPERAND_DIFF` relocation-payload demotions on functions that reference the same object, i.e. they are exact TODAY against the section-symbol relocation form. The open question, never measured, is whether those 6 are exact against the section form by accident of our reconstruction or because the retail object genuinely used it -- if the former, converting the whole TU's model of this object to the external form could hold do_players' +0.2998 AND re-close all six, which is a net project win rather than a trade.
